a.note: Supported by the items, but the last sentences overstated 186(h): the Court does not say the 65 lakh became 'deleted' at final publication, and in paras 10.9 to 10.14 it uses 'excluded' for them and 'deleted' only for the 3.66 lakh. Para 139 added for 'operative act of deletion'.

fix.text: Not at the draft stage. In the Act and the Rules, deletion is an order of the electoral registration officer removing an entry already in the roll: under section 22(c) on an application (Form 7, rule 26) or on the officer's own motion, and during a revision under rule 21A, or on a Form 7 objection decided under rules 17 to 20. Form 7 is one way to start a deletion, not the only one, since section 22 and rule 21A also let the officer act on his own motion. The SIR orders say that electors whose enumeration forms were not returned 'can not be included' or 'will not be included in the draft roll', and the Commission's own lists call this 'non-inclusion'. The Supreme Court held on 27 May 2026 (para 134 and 142) that this 'non-inclusion is not tantamount to a final deletion, but is only a provisional step'. So the plain legal description of the roughly 65 lakh in Bihar at the draft is 'not included in the draft roll'. The same judgment, however, treats the SIR as Rule 21A's exercise of deletion spread over stages beginning with enumeration (para 141), places 'the operative act of deletion' at the end, after enquiry and hearing (para 139), and calls the outcome 'deletions' (para 144 and 186(d)). Its final order speaks of persons 'erroneously deleted on the ground that they are absent, dead, shifted or in duplication' (para 186(h)), the labels the BLOs gave unreturned forms, without saying it means only them. In its own narrative the Court keeps 'excluded' for the 65 lakh (para 10.9, 10.10) and 'deleted' for the 3.66 lakh struck off after the draft (para 10.14).

b.note: Rule 18 lets a Form 7 objection during a revision be allowed without inquiry or Form 14 notice if nobody demands an inquiry, so 'needs notice ... and a summary inquiry' overstated rules 19 and 20. The speaking order is Guidelines para 5(b); 11(d) gives the hearing and appeal, not an order. 'No individual notice, hearing or order before the draft' is an inference from the absence of any such step in the order and guidelines; the Court (para 143) mentions individualised enquiry only 'in cases of doubt'.

fix.text: Names not carried into the draft: no individual notice, hearing or order before the draft. The lists of these names, with the BLO's 'probable reasons', are published (letter of 27.10.2025 para 2(a); Supreme Court order of 14.08.2025 para 3). The elector's remedy is a claim for inclusion in Form 6 with the declaration during the claims period (Guidelines para 4(c); order of 14.08.2025 para 3(vii)). Names on the draft that are then removed, whether on a Form 7 objection or on the officer's own enquiry: an inquiry and a fair and reasonable opportunity (order of 24.06.2025 para 14), a hearing and a written or speaking order (PIB 01.08.2025; Guidelines para 5(b) for the speaking order and 11(d) for the hearing), and appeal to the District Magistrate under section 24(a), then to the Chief Electoral Officer under section 24(b) (order para 14). Under the Rules, a Form 7 objection during a revision may be allowed without inquiry after a week on the list if nobody demands an inquiry (rule 18); where it goes to inquiry, the person objected to gets notice in Form 14 and a summary inquiry where they can be heard (rules 19 and 20), with appeal under rule 23. A deletion on the officer's own motion before final publication needs a published list and notice, consideration of objections, and a chance to show cause for non-residence or ineligibility (rule 21A). Outside a revision, a deletion under section 22 needs a hearing for non-residence or ineligibility (section 22 proviso, which does not cover death) and is appealable under section 24. The Supreme Court held that the SIR's distributed procedure satisfies Rule 21A in substance (para 140 to 144).

c.note: Core finding holds: the orders keep 'not included'/'non-inclusion' apart from 'delete'; the 30.09.2025 table says 'removed' for both; the judgment uses 'excluded' (10.9, 10.10, 137) and 'deletion(s)' (129 heading 'removal of names', 141, 144, 186(d), 186(h)). Two qualifications added: point 4 of the same 30.09.2025 release says 'names not included in draft roll', and 186(h) does not say it refers to the 65 lakh. Also note Guidelines 5(b) uses 'should not be deleted' for proposed electors already on the draft, which is consistent with the orders keeping the words apart.

fix.text: Yes, both blur it in places. The Commission's orders keep the words apart: 'not included in the draft roll' and 'non-inclusion' for unreturned forms, and 'delete any entry from the draft roll' only for names that appeared in the draft (order of 24.06.2025 para 13 and 14; letter of 27.10.2025 para 2(a)). But the summary table of its press release of 30.09.2025 uses one word for both, 'Total Electors removed from Draft List 65 lakhs' and 'Ineligible Electors removed from draft list 3.66 lakhs', although point 4 of the same release calls the first group 'names not included in draft roll'. In October 2026 its counsel told the Bombay High Court, as PTI reported, that absence from the draft is not deletion. The Supreme Court's order of 14.08.2025 says 'not included' and 'non-inclusion'. Its judgment of 27.05.2026 uses 'excluded from the draft roll' (para 10.9, 10.10, 137) and holds non-inclusion is not a final deletion (para 134, 142). But it also frames the issue as 'removal of names' tested against Rule 21A (heading E.3.2, para 129), describes the SIR as Rule 21A's 'exercise of deletion' distributed across stages beginning with enumeration (para 141), and in its operative conclusions calls the results 'deletions' (para 144, 186(d)) and speaks of names 'erroneously deleted on the ground that they are absent, dead, shifted or in duplication' (para 186(h)), the BLOs' labels for unreturned forms, though it does not say it means only those names. Its narrative keeps 'excluded' for the 65 lakh and 'deleted' for the 3.66 lakh (para 10.9, 10.14). The site can say 'not included in the draft' or 'left off the draft' for the draft stage with the orders' and the Court's support, and 'excluded' is the Court's own word. It should not say the authorities never call these deletions: the Supreme Court calls the SIR's outcome 'deletions' and the Commission's table says 'removed'.
